archetype.name: Fringe Contender (run-first)
archetype.definition: A team with a top-three rushing attack and a solid per-play defense that keeps beating itself with turnovers and sacks, good enough to hang around a soft NFC South but not yet good enough to separate from it.

report.headline: A real run game and sturdy defense, undone by turnovers and quarterback chaos.
report.take:
Atlanta is a ground-and-defense team stuck inside a turnover problem. Kevin Stefanski's offense leans on the run harder than almost anyone, with a pass rate over expected of -8.3 (29th), and the run game earns it. Bijan Robinson carries the load with Brian Robinson behind him, and the Falcons rank 2nd in yards per carry (5.1) and 3rd in rush EPA. On the other side, the defense is better than its scoreboard: 11th in EPA allowed, 6th in success rate allowed, 8th against the run and 4th against deep passes.

The record of 2-4 comes from three things. The first is the quarterback carousel. Cooper Rush started Week 1 and Tua Tagovailoa started Week 2, and those two games produced -15.8 and -25.1 passing EPA, including a five-turnover 34-3 home loss to Carolina. That is most of why the pass offense ranks 29th. The second is giveaways: 12 turnovers against 5 takeaways, a -7 margin. The third is close games: Atlanta is winless in one-score games. Special teams (27th) haven't helped either. The point differential implies 2.6 wins, so the record is only slightly unlucky. This is roughly the team the numbers say it is.

The season splits at Week 3. Michael Penix Jr. won his first two starts going away, 35-14 at Green Bay and 45-24 in New Orleans, with positive passing and rushing EPA in both. Then the run game cooled sharply, from 242 and 205 yards to 110 against Baltimore and 63 against Chicago. Without it the offense turned back into the turnover-and-sack version: five sacks and three giveaways against the Bears. The line rarely allows pressure (2nd in pressure rate) and the ball comes out fast, yet the sack rate is 26th. When protection breaks down, it ends in a sack.

The history is the warning. Atlanta has spent most of the last eight seasons at seven or eight wins with a negative wins-over-expected, and nothing here yet breaks that pattern. The division is the opening: Carolina leads at 3-2 and four division games remain. The path to a winning season requires Penix to keep the pass game positive when the run is bottled up, and the last two weeks say he hasn't solved that yet.

strengths.title: A top-three rushing attack
strengths.body: Atlanta ranks 2nd in yards per carry, 3rd in rush EPA and 3rd in run success, with a low stuff rate behind a line that also takes few penalties. This is structural, built on Bijan Robinson's volume and a line that opens lanes, not on game script, since the team has trailed plenty. Expect it to hold up over the season, though the last two weeks show it can be shut down by good fronts.

strengths.title: Per-play defense better than points
strengths.body: The defense ranks 11th in EPA allowed and 6th in success rate allowed, stops the run and almost never gets beaten deep. Points allowed (23rd) are inflated by short fields off 12 offensive turnovers, including the five-giveaway Carolina game. If ball security normalizes even a little, the scoring defense should move toward its per-play level.

strengths.title: Penix has lifted the passing floor
strengths.body: The 29th-ranked pass offense is mostly a hangover from the Rush and Tagovailoa starts. Penix posted positive passing EPA in three of his four starts and has thrown for 944 yards. The Chicago game, with -9.8 passing EPA, is the reminder that this is a young quarterback still learning to win when the run is shut down.

concerns.title: Turnovers are the whole story
concerns.body: A turnover margin of -0.8 per game (26th) has wrecked a team that is close to average per play. Atlanta has given it away 12 times, with multi-turnover games against Pittsburgh, Carolina and Chicago, and has not produced takeaways in return (22nd). Part of this is quarterback churn that should fade with Penix settled, but the Bears game shows it hasn't gone away.

concerns.title: Pressure rarely comes, but becomes sacks
concerns.body: The line allows the 2nd-lowest pressure rate and the ball comes out quickly, yet the sack rate is 26th and 16 sacks have been taken. That points to the quarterbacks and the route structure as much as the blockers: when the first read isn't there, the play dies. It matters most when the run game stalls and the offense has to drop back.

concerns.title: Defense leaks on money downs
concerns.body: Despite strong early-down numbers, the defense is 23rd on third down and 21st in red-zone touchdown rate, and it is winless in close games. This is the gap between a decent defense and one that wins games. It is now worse with injuries at cornerback and linebacker heading into the toughest stretch of the schedule.

trend.note: The season moved from two ugly quarterback-carousel losses, to two dominant Penix wins built on 200-yard rushing days, to two losses where the run game faded and the turnovers returned. The arrow over the last two weeks points down.

nextGame.headline: Atlanta's ground game runs into an unbeaten 49ers' elite run front.
nextGame.body:
This is a bad stylistic draw for Atlanta. San Francisco is 6-0 and first in net EPA, and its defense is 2nd against the run and 1st in explosive runs allowed. That is exactly the strength the Falcons build around. Where the 49ers give ground is underneath: they rank 21st in short-pass EPA allowed, which suits Penix's quick game if he can stay on schedule. On the other side, Brock Purdy's passing offense ranks 1st in EPA, and his line allows the lowest sack rate in the league. Atlanta's pass rush gets home on hits more than sacks, so it needs takeaways rather than drive-killing sacks. The Book has San Francisco -3.5 with a 49.5 total, and Atlanta is +170.

Availability cuts both ways. The 49ers will be without edge rusher Nick Bosa and safety Marques Sigle (an 88% snap player), Deebo Samuel and Christian Kirk are out, and Mike Evans is doubtful. That thins the receiving corps around Purdy. Atlanta has its own secondary problem: cornerback C.J. Henderson is out, nickel corner Billy Bowman Jr. is questionable with a hamstring, and linebackers Divine Deablo (arm) and Kendal Daniels (carted off with a neck injury) are both questionable. That is a lot of coverage snaps in doubt against the league's best passing offense.

waysToWin.title: Quick game against soft underneath zones
waysToWin.body: The 49ers allow positive EPA on short throws (21st), and Atlanta's offense is built on getting the ball out fast. Feeding Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Bijan Robinson on short timing throws can replace the run game as the chain-mover. It also blunts a pass rush that ranks 5th in pressure rate even with Bosa inactive.

waysToWin.title: Squeeze a depleted receiving corps
waysToWin.body: With Samuel and Kirk out and Evans doubtful, Purdy is working with a thin set of receivers. Atlanta's defense is 4th in deep-pass EPA allowed and 6th in QB hit rate. If it takes away explosives and stops the run (8th in rush EPA allowed), San Francisco has to drive the length of the field with backups, which creates chances for the defense.

waysToWin.title: Win the turnover battle for once
waysToWin.body: Atlanta's two wins came in games with one turnover or fewer, and both teams' special teams rank near the bottom, so field position may come down to giveaways. San Francisco is +0.8 per game in turnover margin. A clean game from Penix makes this a coin flip rather than a 3.5-point dog.

waysToLose.title: Purdy picks apart a patched secondary
waysToLose.body: San Francisco's passing offense is 1st in EPA and 1st in success rate, and its line has allowed only 3 sacks all year. With Henderson out and Bowman and the starting linebackers questionable, Atlanta's third-down weakness (23rd) becomes a real liability. Lead backs have also hurt this defense in the passing game, and that remains a safe outlet for Purdy even without his top wideouts.

waysToLose.title: Run game stalls, offense goes one-dimensional
waysToLose.body: The 49ers allow the 2nd-lowest rush EPA and the fewest explosive runs in the league. If Bijan Robinson is held down the way Chicago held this offense to 63 rushing yards, Atlanta has to throw on obvious passing downs. That is where its sack and turnover problems live, and an early deficit makes it worse.

waysToLose.title: Sacks and giveaways hand over short fields
waysToLose.body: San Francisco ranks 5th in pressure rate, and Atlanta's sack rate (26th) shows how often pressure becomes a lost down. Add a quarterback who turned it over three times last week and the Falcons' defense ends up defending short fields, which is how its points allowed got to 25.5 per game.

nextGame.watch: Atlanta's early-down rushing success against the 49ers' front: if the Falcons stay ahead of the chains, Penix can play the quick game; if not, the sacks and turnovers come back.

restOfSeason.body:
The underlying team is roughly average: a top-five run game, a top-12 per-play defense, a bottom-five passing offense and poor special teams. The record should drift toward the point differential rather than far past it. Some regression in Atlanta's favor is due. A turnover margin this negative rarely persists at this level, and with Penix entrenched the quarterback-carousel disasters shouldn't repeat. That should pull points allowed down toward what the per-play defense suggests. What won't return is the 200-yard rushing pace of Weeks 3 and 4, which came against softer run defenses. And whether Penix can carry drives when the run is stopped is still unproven.

The schedule is lopsided. The next month includes San Francisco, Kansas City and Minnesota, all unbeaten, plus Cincinnati. The back end is far softer: Tampa Bay twice (30th on offense), Washington, New Orleans and Detroit's 32nd-ranked defense. With Carolina leading the division at only 3-2 and four division games left, a 2-5 or 3-6 start doesn't end the race. But the realistic ceiling is the kind of 7-8 win season this franchise has posted for years, not a breakout.
swingFactors: Penix's turnover rate when the run game is contained
Health of the cornerbacks and linebackers Deablo and Daniels
Results in four remaining NFC South games

confidence.note: Six games with three different starting quarterbacks; only four with Penix, and the per-play picture is clearer than the record.
